messages:
alex: Heads-up — longctx load test shows KV-cache memory growth and repeated page-table (PT) reclaim cycles. H100 runs worse than A100; we're seeing paging spikes and SLA violations. Anyone else seeing continuous reclaim/fragmentation?

tara: I remember similar drift with sweepback heuristics. Can you paste the perf traces / small repro? :eyes:

alex: Pasting trimmed trace snippets and a short trace log: ```
[trace] evict_loop enter ts=0x7f  evict_count=0
[trace] page_free_list=1024 -> 18  (many tiny fragments)
[trace] kernel_select=tiling_v2 (H100)  seq_len=2048
[trace] evict_kernel_launch_ms=12 -> 38 -> 120 (spike correlated with pagewalks)
[trace] l2_miss_rate spike at reclaim windows
```

jia: That pattern smells like reverse-sweepback remap creating lots of small free segments. Free-list gets splintered, then reclaim runs repeatedly because the coalescer never sees adjacent segments. Which kernel was chosen on A100 vs H100?

alex: On the failing H100 jobs kernel_select logs show `tiling_v2` (optim for tiled kernels). On A100 we fall back to `linear_v1`. Batch distribution matters: most traffic is batch=1-2 (PLG traces).

sam: Two quick hypotheses: 1) kernel selection (tiling_v2) has different allocation/grain alignment that prevents coalescing; 2) batching heuristics producing lots of tiny KV inserts so pages never fill and we fragment. Can you share batch histogram?

alex: Batch histogram from the run: `P(1)=62%, P(2)=22%, P(>4)=6%`. Batching mode is latency-first (small batches favored). Repro command below: ```
# repro: longctx-run with tracing
KV_PAGED=1 KV_RECLAIM_THRESHOLD=0.65 KV_COALESCE_ENABLED=1 
./tools/run_longctx.sh --model paged-attn --seq 2048 --duration 15m --trace kv,pt,allocator
```

jia: I ran a short reproduction and saw exactly the free-list shrink/gap pattern. NV counters: `l2_cache_misses` and `page_table_walks` spike during reclaim. Coalescer isn't merging because alignment differs between page sizes used by tiling_v2.

tara: On H100 the allocator uses 64k-aligned tiles for tiled kernels; that means the page coalescer logic (which expects 4k alignment) fails to merge. That could explain fragmentation. MI250X also shows a different preferred page size and has its own kernel choice.

maria: Quick product note — the demo cluster hit a 99.9->99.5% SLA blip last night when this started. Customers noticed higher tail latency. We need a mitigation fast.

sam: Mitigations we can try immediately: 1) raise reclaim threshold (less aggressive reclaim churn), 2) disable sweepback compaction on H100 (force simpler free path), 3) force linear kernel selection as fallback for small-batch workloads. I'll open a short PR for (2) + (1).

alex: I pushed a small branch that disables sweepback on devices with tiling kernel selected: internal link: https://redwood.internal/pr/kv-sweepback-h100. CI will run perf tests.

infra-bot: CI: kv-longctx-regress test: 3 failures. Artifacts uploaded: https://ci.redwood/internal/4923456780/artifacts (traces + perf).

jia: I'll bisect the kernel selector to see when coalescer assumptions broke. Also testing forcing `KV_COALESCE_ENABLED=0` as a potential workaround to avoid bad partial merges inducing thrash. Planning to run cross-arch: A100 / H100 / MI250X over 2h.

tara: Quick note from local run: bumping reclaim threshold to 0.8 reduced reclaim frequency but increased peak memory (expected). It stabilized SLA for 30m synthetic streams. We should A/B test tradeoffs.

sam: Agree. For Dedicated customers we can offer a config knob (latency vs cost) while we fix coalescer/kernelselect logic.

alex: Action items: 
- jia: bisect kernelselector + test coalescer off on MI250X (ETA 24h)
- sam: open patch to fall back to linear kernel for batch<4 on tiling devices (PR opened)
- tara: run 2h longctx with reclaim=0.8 to collect memory growth numbers

maria: Please keep me posted, I'll notify support and flag the impacted demos.

jia: starting bisect now. I'll post results and minimal repro in #eng-runtime when done. :thumbsup:

tara: :eyes: ping if you want a pair on traces.

alex: thanks everyone. I'll keep the PR linked and monitor CI.
